Subject: Capacity need for Nov product launch - observed sustained peaks

Hi Sergio,

Quick note from our ops team — we're seeing higher-than-expected sustained GPU demand ahead of our public launch (targeting mid-November). Attached is a cleaned export of October usage (novacorp_oct_usage.csv). High-level: average committed pool utilization during peak windows is ~67%, with sustained spikes to 92% on heavy inference batches (these spikes are lasting multiple hours on launch rehearsal days). We're seeing queued requests and tail latency creep on p95.

Can you recommend a pragmatic short-term capacity plan we can commit to now (we'd rather avoid a week-by-week bandaid) and an expected lead time to provision reserved GPUs in our us region? Also send ballpark economics so procurement can evaluate.

Attachments: novacorp_oct_usage.csv (CSV)

Thanks,
Samir Patel
VP, ML Operations
NovaCorp

Subject: Re: Capacity need for Nov product launch - observed sustained peaks

Hi Samir — thanks for the data, and great context. I pulled the attached report (novacorp_oct_usage.csv) into our capacity model and ran two scenario projections. Short answer: we can meet the launch with a targeted reserved add-on plus a short trial period to validate assumptions. Details below. Attached: mutual_action_plan_v2.docx (MMP + provisioning timeline).

Summary of what I see from your export:
- Current committed pool: 40 A100-equivalent slots (dedicated).
- Observed peak sustained utilization: 67% average with spikes up to 92%.
- Observed tail: p95 token latency increases ~1.9x when queueing begins.

Options (with expected impact and lead time):
1) Option A — Conservative add: +6 A100-equivalent reserved GPUs (incremental)
   - Expected effect: sustained utilization drops to ~52% at current traffic; p95 latency reduction ~25-30%.
   - Lead time to provision: 5-7 business days after signed amendment.
   - Monthly committed delta: ~$5,500/GPU × 6 = $33,000/mo (we can offer a 40% trial discount for first 90 days).

2) Option B — Headroom add: +12 A100-equivalent reserved GPUs
   - Expected effect: headroom ~25%, supports 6-9 months of growth without further reserve adds, p95 latency reduction ~40% at current peak.
   - Lead time: 10 business days for tranching & placement.
   - Monthly committed delta: ~$66,000/mo (discounts available for annual commit).

Recommendation: start with Option A on a 90-day trial (convert to full commit or expand to Option B if utilization stays above projection). That balances cost and risk while getting you through launch.

Next steps I propose:
- I will draft a short commit addendum for +6 GPUs with a 90-day trial discount (Ben can confirm pricing and DocuSign flow).
- Once signed, operations will schedule provisioning and confirm the exact provisioning slot IDs + region mapping (us-east).
- We'll add basic observability hooks in Redwood Console for token-level cost/latency alerts tied to the launch prompts so we can decide quickly if we need to escalate to +12.

Attached: mutual_action_plan_v2.docx (proposed MMP + provisioning checklist).
